mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES continues rising from its near-zero baseline, commuting-linked foot traffic should spill into nearby retail visits and lift RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The effect is strongest when TRANSIT is flat or improving, because workers can actually reach commercial areas.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES turned positive in t-1w and t-0w while TRANSIT moved toward zero
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not exceed the prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES remaining above 0 for at least two weeks and TRANSIT not deteriorating.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in RESIDENTIAL time suppresses discretionary out-of-home shopping; when people spend more time at home, retail and recreation visits fall over the following one to two weeks. This mechanism predicts lower RETAIL_REC unless other mobility channels rise enough to offset the stay-at-home effect.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL remains elevated at 4-6 points above baseline across all four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above the last 4-week mean within 14 days while RESIDENTIAL stays at or above its current elevated range.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM stays very high, routine errand traffic can be substituted away from discretionary retail, so RETAIL_REC drifts lower over the next month. The signal becomes actionable only if grocery mobility remains above roughly 35 points for consecutive weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stays above 35 for at least 2 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM is above 39 in all four weeks and above 42 in the last two weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days even though GROCERY_PHARM remains above 35 for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A recovery in PARKS after a short dip signals more leisure circulation and spillover trips to retail and recreation, lifting RETAIL_REC within one week. The mechanism is strongest when PARKS moves up from a depressed level and does not reverse immediately.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by at least 5 points from its prior week after being below -15
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS rebounded from -21.1 in t-2w to -16.9 in t-1w before easing again
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 7 days after PARKS increases by 5 points from a sub -15 level.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT is recovering while WORKPLACES are also positive, the city is in a mobility-normalization regime that should support more shopping trips and higher RETAIL_REC over four weeks. The mechanism fails when transit gains occur without workplace recovery, because then trips are more likely to be non-retail.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -3.4 to -0.7 while WORKPLACES moved from -2.0 to 1.4
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains at or below the prior 4-week mean over the next 28 days even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES are both positive for at least two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in RETAIL_REC itself can persist through short-run habit formation: weak retail demand in the last week predicts another week of softness unless an external mobility rebound appears. This is a one-week momentum signal rather than a structural trend.
candidate_trigger: RETAIL_REC falls below -2 after being above -2 in the prior week
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC moved from -1.7 in t-1w to -1.9 in t-0w after two earlier weeks near -3
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC turns upward in the next 7 days after a sub -2 print, with no concurrent rise in WORKPLACES or TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: If parks mobility remains seasonally depressed while workplace and transit mobility are near baseline, late-summer outdoor substitution is weak and retail visits should stay soft over the next month. The mechanism is specific to periods when PARKS stays below -15 without a compensating leisure rebound.
candidate_trigger: PARKS remains below -15 for 3 consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS is below -15 in all four weeks while TRANSIT is near zero
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last 4-week average over the next 28 days even though PARKS stays below -15 for three straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A broad loosening regime that leaves RESIDENTIAL elevated but pushes WORKPLACES and TRANSIT upward should eventually pull consumers back into retail corridors, producing higher RETAIL_REC over two to four weeks. If workplace and transit do not rise together, the residential pullback does not translate into retail demand.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL stays above 4
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is persistently above 4 while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT have recently improved
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase within 14 days after simultaneous week-on-week gains in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT with RESIDENTIAL still above 4.
